I took over the unfinished goal-1 work, made the harness coherent, and re-ran the full Windows matrix on Gerald between 03:09Z and 04:37Z on 2026-10-28. Cameras: C922, C930e and the generic 4C4A:4A55. The Kiyo was never opened.

The 2026-10-25 raw captures were re-validated with the same validator into mjpeg_resummarized_20261025_data{,_b}/. The cell-by-cell comparison is in compare_vs_20261025.json. mjpeg/RESULTS.md has the matrix and findings.

**MF IMFSourceReader, native MJPG** (converters disabled, output subtype verified MJPG):
- 100% valid JPEG on all three cameras at 720p30 and 1080p30.
- Frame rate: C922 30.00, C930e 30.05, generic 25.76–25.78 fps.
- Process CPU: 0.7–2.2% of one core per camera.

**PyAV dshow vcodec=mjpeg passthrough:**
- The full header bytes (SOI to SOS) are byte-identical to MF for every camera and mode. For the generic camera, which changes its quantisation tables between frames, all 11–14 distinct headers per window appear in both.
- Dominant table fingerprints are identical between 10-25 and 10-27 in all 11 matched rows.
- CPU: 0.9–1.6% for one camera.

**Generic camera frame rate.** It runs at about 25.7 fps on every native-MJPG path, in daylight on 10-25 and in the dark tonight, with manual exposure and AE priority 0. Low light does not explain it. Its 30 fps under OpenCV MSMF is padding: 48 of about 300 frames repeat the previous frame, so the unique rate is 25.3–25.4 fps.

**Three cameras at once.** The C930e and the generic camera share a hub and cannot both stream:
- MF: ReadSample fails with 0x800718CF, which is Win32 6351, "camera interface doesn't have the desired bandwidth".
- DirectShow: the generic camera's open fails with OSError 5.

**WinRT MediaFrameReader with MJPG subtype:** E_INVALIDARG on every acquire, on all three cameras and in every variant. With no subtype it delivers only decoded NV12.

**OpenCV 4.12 never returns JPEG bytes:**
- DSHOW decode costs 25–28% of one core at 720p and 37–40% at 1080p.
- MSMF opens take about 40 s on the Logitech cameras. MSMF decode costs 46–54% at 720p and 143–156% at 1080p.
- MSMF FORMAT=-1 returns NV12 pixels, not JPEG.

**Corrections to earlier claims:**
- OpenCV MSMF "0 frames" was a harness bug: the script waited only 30 s for an open that takes about 40 s. Fixed with `--open-wait`.
- OpenCV DSHOW CONVERT_RGB=0 "10 fps YUY2" depends on the property order. With size-first order it negotiates MJPG at 30 fps, but the frames are still BGR.
- MF capture metadata (the 32-byte UVC header) is now present on the C922 and C930e. That matches the registry value set after the 10-25 run.

**Other:**
- Several CPU% numbers are 1.3–2.3x those of 10-25 even at low machine load. They are labelled, and the ranking is unchanged.
- Linux and macOS drafts pass static checks (all_ok), write to fresh run roots, and have one runner per OS. They are still unrun on those OSes.

- OS timestamps sit on the 16.0 ms grid on all three cameras, including the generic one.

- C922 clocks: SOF 884.7-885.0 counts per host second; STC-PTS 33.0 ms; PTS period alternates ~9.92M/10.08M ticks.
- Rolling-shutter slope 30.1-31.5 ms per frame height.

rerun.summary:
Every earlier usbvideo bandwidth claim that could be re-tested without WinUSB or admin was re-run. The hardware claims hold.

What was confirmed:
- **Topology:** unchanged. The C922 is alone on xHCI root port 1. The C930e and the generic camera share the Genesys 05e3:0610 hub behind root port 13. The alt tables are identical.
- **Alt selection:** usbvideo selected exactly the same alt setting in all 32 single-camera modes that also ran on 2026-10-25 (C922 9, C930e 9 + 10 small modes, generic 4). It is always the camera's large request.
- **Shared-hub threshold:** C930e alt 8 + generic passes; alt 9 + generic fails with 0x800718CF. With a 2.5 s stagger this held in 3 separate batches (r07, rv, rc). The 194f:0422 audio device had no iso pipes open before and after.
- **Budget model:** hs_budget_model.py agrees on 26/26 shared-hub combos in the re-run. Re-run on the original data, it reproduces the earlier 14/14 file byte-identically.
- **Different root ports do not compete:** C922 alt 11 + C930e alt 11 streamed together twice. C922 alt 11 + C930e alt 8 + generic alt 1 all streamed at full rate.
- **No fps loss:** every stream that started ran at its nominal rate (C922 ~30, C930e ~30, generic 25.7-25.8).

What changed:
- **Simultaneous start (stagger 0, b05):** in 3 of 4 over-budget combos a different camera lost than on 2026-10-25. Who loses then depends on a start race; only the staggered start order is deterministic.
- **Bytes/s and headroom ratios shifted:** C930e 720p30 6.0x -> 6.6x, C922 720p30 4.4x -> 5.3x, generic 640x480 69.9x -> 52.2x. Scenes were dark for the C922 (luma ~17.6) and generic (~20-22) and monitor-lit for the C930e (~77-95). Earlier runs recorded no luma, so the shift cannot be attributed. Exposure was forced to manual -7 in every run, so light cannot explain any fps difference.

New findings:
1. **Generic camera 1080p MJPEG:** 385/385 frames (3 runs) fail libjpeg-turbo strict decode with ~400-490 "extraneous bytes before EOI". The marker walk and Pillow pass, and EOI is present, so the frames are complete, not truncated. Its first frame at 720p failed the same way in 2 of ~13 streams. All 8224 saved frames pass the marker walk and Pillow; 8095 also pass strict decode.
2. **C930e MJPEG 640x480@15:** it sometimes sends bursts at 30 fps cadence (32 ms intervals). This explains steady-fps outliers of 16.99 (2026-10-25) and 19.46 (tonight). It is not a bandwidth effect.
3. **C922 1080p@5:** the earlier 15.76 fps outlier did not reproduce; tonight it gave 5.01 fps at the same alt 5.

Analysis scripts: coexist_summarize.py re-run on the phase-2 raw data reproduces all 4 earlier coexist JSONs exactly.

Skipped: everything that needs WinUSB/libuvc (coexist_hold.sh and the verify/*.sh holds), ETW (needs elevation), and anything touching the Kiyo.

verdicts.reason: Every ksvideosrc run reached the Kiyo: gst_ks attempt 1 at 03:16Z, ks_tbp at 03:27Z and gst_ks at 03:37Z. In GStreamer 1.28.8, gst_ks_video_src_open_device (gstksvideosrc.c:445) calls ks_video_device_list_sort_cameras_first before it matches device-name. That function calls ks_video_device_entry_decide_priority (ksvideohelpers.c), which does CreateFile(GENERIC_READ|GENERIC_WRITE) on every KS video-capture filter path and queries its property sets. The Kiyo's usbvideo filter is one of those paths. So it got an IRP_MJ_CREATE and a KS property IOCTL three times. I checked the other paths at source level and they really are filtered: mfvideosrc device-path calls ActivateObject only on the matched IMFActivate (gstmfsourcereader.cpp:812-827, :292); FFmpeg dshow binds only the matching moniker (dshow.c dshow_cycle_devices); pygrabber binds by index after a BindToStorage enumeration; cv2_enumerate_cameras uses only GetAllocatedString and BindToStorage; dshow_exposure_read binds only allowlisted monikers.

The prior-art rerun numbers mostly hold. I re-ran two tests myself (scope below). But the safety claim is wrong: the run did open the excluded Kiyo, and one drift number is a fitting artifact.
